sourceNote.title: Login rate limiting
sourceNote.html:
Login rate limiting

Exploring the sign-in rate limit on a test environment with a throwaway account (tester@example.test).

  • After 5 failed passwords within 15 minutes for one account, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes.

  • The lock message says "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." and does not reveal whether the account exists.

  • A successful sign-in resets the failed-attempt counter.

  • Unknown email addresses get the same generic error and also count towards a per-IP limit of 20 attempts per 15 minutes.

  • Password reset link still works while locked.

  • Observed: the 5th failure already showed the lock message, so the 5th attempt might count as locked instead of the 6th.

  • Open question: does the lock apply per account across devices?

bodyHtml:
Scenario: Account lock threshold and duration

Test case: Lock begins on the fifth failed password and expires after 15 minutes

Purpose: Detect an off-by-one threshold or an incorrect lock duration.

Preconditions: Test environment; throwaway account has no active lock or recent failed attempts.

Test data: tester@example.test; incorrect password; correct password.

Steps:

  • Submit four incorrect passwords within 15 minutes; verify that sign-in is not yet locked.

  • Submit the fifth incorrect password within the same window; verify the message is “Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.”

  • Attempt sign-in with the correct password just before 15 minutes have elapsed since locking; verify sign-in remains blocked.

  • Attempt sign-in with the correct password after the 15-minute lock has elapsed; verify sign-in succeeds.

Expected result: The fifth failure triggers the stated message, and the lock lasts 15 minutes.

Coverage notes: Preserves the observation that the fifth failure already showed the lock message; confirms whether that attempt actually starts the lock. Assumed failure modes: locking one attempt early or late, and premature or delayed expiry.

Scenario: Failed-attempt counter reset

Test case: Successful sign-in clears earlier failures

Purpose: Detect stale failures remaining after successful authentication.

Preconditions: Throwaway account has no active lock or recent failed attempts; use a fresh per-IP attempt window.

Test data: tester@example.test; incorrect password; correct password.

Steps:

  • Submit four incorrect passwords, then sign in successfully with the correct password.

  • Sign out and submit four more incorrect passwords, keeping all attempts within 15 minutes; verify no account lock occurs.

  • Submit one more incorrect password; verify the lock message appears.

Expected result: Only failures after the successful sign-in count toward the next account lock.

Coverage notes: Grounded in the stated counter reset. Assumed failure mode: earlier failures incorrectly survive a successful sign-in.

Scenario: Unknown addresses and per-IP counting

Test case: Unknown addresses receive generic errors and contribute to the IP limit

Purpose: Detect account-existence disclosure or unknown-address attempts bypassing IP counting.

Preconditions: One test IP with no attempts in the preceding 15 minutes; test email addresses confirmed not to exist.

Test data: tester@example.test with an incorrect password; 20 distinct unknown email addresses; one additional unknown address.

Steps:

  • From the test IP, submit one incorrect password for tester@example.test and record the generic error.

  • Submit attempts for 19 distinct unknown addresses from the same IP within the same 15-minute window; compare their errors with the known-account error and record behavior at the twentieth total attempt.

  • Submit an attempt for another unknown address within that window; verify that the per-IP limit prevents unrestricted further attempts.

Expected result: Unknown addresses receive the same generic error without revealing account existence and count toward the limit of 20 attempts per IP per 15 minutes.

Coverage notes: Assumed failure modes: unknown addresses excluded from counting or distinct addresses bypassing the shared IP limit. The note does not specify the IP-limit message or whether attempt 20 itself is blocked; record that boundary behavior without inventing an expected message.

Scenario: Password reset during account lock

Test case: Password reset link remains usable while sign-in is locked

Purpose: Detect the sign-in lock incorrectly blocking the password reset link.

Preconditions: tester@example.test is locked following five failed passwords within 15 minutes; its password reset link is available.

Test data: Password reset link for tester@example.test.

Steps:

  • Open the password reset link while the account lock is active; verify that the reset flow is accessible.

Expected result: The password reset link still works while sign-in is locked.

Coverage notes: Assumed failure mode: the sign-in lock also blocks reset access. The note does not define whether resetting a password clears the lock.

Scenario: Lock scope across devices

Test case: Check whether switching devices bypasses an account lock

Purpose: Explore the note’s open question about account locks across devices.

Preconditions: Two devices can access the test environment; tester@example.test starts unlocked; per-IP limits are not exhausted.

Test data: tester@example.test; incorrect password on device A; correct password on device B.

Steps:

  • On device A, submit five incorrect passwords within 15 minutes and verify the lock message appears.

  • While that lock is active, attempt sign-in on device B with the correct password; record whether sign-in is blocked and which message appears.

Expected result: Under the assumption that the lock applies per account across devices, device B also blocks sign-in. The note explicitly leaves this behavior unresolved, so the observation requires requirement confirmation before a pass/fail decision.

Coverage notes: Assumed failure mode: device-local lock enforcement permits a locked account to sign in elsewhere.
